findings.title: Default 'Kalman' forecaster ALWAYS returns a constant flat-line forecast - EM never fits the transition/observation matrices
findings.description: kalman.fitter() calls pykalman KalmanFilter(n_dim_obs=d, n_dim_state=d).em(x, n_iter=n_iter) without em_vars, so pykalman's default em_vars only optimizes covariances + initial state; the transition and observation matrices remain IDENTITY. Iterating filter_update with no observations therefore repeats the last filtered state forever: hyp.predict()'s DEFAULT model produces a mathematically constant forecast for EVERY dataset. Verified: flat on a strong noisy sine, flat on a linear trend (does not continue the slope), flat on a 2-column sin/cos rotation (forecast stds 0.0 / 2.3e-16), and n_iter=25 does not help (forecast std 5.7e-17). There is no way to fix it through the API: fitter() only reads n_iter, and unknown kwargs are silently ignored (em_vars= would be a no-op). Counterfactual proof that the fix works: fitting the same pykalman model with em_vars including 'transition_matrices'/'observation_matrices' on the sin/cos data learns a rotation matrix [[0.975,0.156],[-0.153,0.975]] and forecasts with corr 0.988 vs held-out truth. Compounding: (a) the Kalman class docstring FALSELY states n_iter is the 'Number of EM iterations used to fit the transition/observation matrices and their noise covariances'; (b) the shipped tutorial docs/tutorials/projectile_kalman.ipynb forecasts projectile motion via hyp.predict(first30, model='Kalman', t=HORIZON), which returns a flat line for a parabolic trajectory; (c) tests/predict/test_kalman.py::test_trend_direction_sanity compares the forecast mean against df['a'].iloc[:35] (the FIRST half - its comment says 'second half'), so a flat forecast at the last value trivially passes.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
t = np.arange(180)
sine = pd.DataFrame({'y': np.sin(2*np.pi*t/40.0) + 0.1*rng.standard_normal(180)})
fc, m = hyp.predict(sine, model='Kalman', t=20, return_model=True)
kf = m.models_[0]['kf']
print('transition:', np.asarray(kf.transition_matrices))
print('unique forecast values:', fc['y'].nunique())
"
findings.expected: A fitted linear-Gaussian state-space model whose learned dynamics continue the oscillation (docstring: EM fits the transition/observation matrices); at minimum a non-constant forecast on a strong sine or trend.
findings.actual: transition_matrices: [[1.]]  observation_matrices: [[1.]]  forecast unique values: 1  (first3 = [0.24, 0.24, 0.24]; fc_std/train_std = 0.0 on sine, trend, and 2-D rotation data; n_iter=25 forecast std 5.695e-17)

findings.title: pandas Series input crashes with a cryptic IndexError (wrangled to an empty (0,0) DataFrame)
findings.description: A pandas Series is the most natural container for a univariate timeseries, but dw.wrangle(pd.Series(...)) returns a (0,0) DataFrame, so resolve_t hits index[-1] on an empty index and hyp.predict crashes with 'IndexError: index -1 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0' - no mention of the input type or how to fix it (.to_frame()). Root cause is in datawrangler's funnel, but hyp.predict is the user-facing surface; it should either forecast the Series or reject it with a clear message.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
y = np.sin(np.arange(100)/5.0)
hyp.predict(pd.Series(y, name='y'), model='Laplace', t=4)
"
findings.expected: A (4,1) forecast (Series treated as one univariate dataset), or a clear TypeError naming pandas Series and suggesting .to_frame().
findings.actual: IndexError: index -1 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0  (dw.wrangle(Series) shape: (0, 0))

findings.title: 1-D numpy array input is silently treated as ONE observation with n features - returns a (t, n) nonsense forecast
findings.description: hyp.predict(np.sin(np.arange(100)/5.0), t=4) does not forecast the 100-step series: dw.wrangle turns the 1-D array into a (1,100) DataFrame (one observation, 100 features), so the result is a (4,100) 'forecast' extrapolated from a single observation - meaningless values, no warning. The docstring advertises 'DataFrame/array or list of these', and a 1-D array is the most common way scientists hold a univariate series. Workaround (.reshape(-1,1)) works but nothing tells the user. Same mechanism makes a plain python list of floats come back as a LIST of per-scalar forecasts.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
y = np.sin(np.arange(100)/5.0)
print(hyp.predict(y, model='Laplace', t=4).shape)   # (4, 100) !!
print(hyp.predict(y.reshape(-1,1), model='Laplace', t=4).shape)  # (4, 1) correct
"
findings.expected: (4, 1) - the 1-D array interpreted as a 100-observation univariate series (or at least a loud warning about the (1,100) interpretation).
findings.actual: (4, 100)  - forecast of 100 'features' conditioned on a single observation; silent.

findings.title: datetime horizon exactly equal to the last timestamp crashes with a cryptic pandas ValueError
findings.description: resolve_t documents 'If t is at or before the last observation ... a negative count is returned, meaning truncate'. For t strictly before the last observation truncation works, but for t == index[-1] resolve_t returns n_steps=0 with future_index = the ENTIRE past index; Forecaster.predict then skips the truncation branch (n_steps < 0 is False) and calls the forecaster with n_steps=0, which builds a 0-row values array against a full-length index -> 'ValueError: Length of values (0) does not match length of index (N)'. Affects every model. Programmatically computed targets (e.g. forecast every subject to a common end time) will hit this whenever one dataset already reaches the target.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame({'a': np.arange(10.0)}, index=pd.date_range('2026-01-01', periods=10, freq='D'))
hyp.predict(df, model='Laplace', t=df.index[-1])
"
findings.expected: Truncation semantics per the resolve_t docstring: return the dataset unchanged (sliced up to t == last), like any past t.
findings.actual: ValueError: Length of values (0) does not match length of index (10)   [resolve_t returned n_steps=0, len(future_index)=10]

findings.title: ARIMA default order (1,1,1) cannot extrapolate trends (flat forecast on a linear trend) and damps oscillations (sine corr 0.46)
findings.description: With the default order=(1,1,1) and no trend term, the ARIMA forecast of a clean linear trend is essentially constant (forecast std / train std = 0.0004; corr with held-out truth -0.239) - visually a horizontal red line while the data keeps climbing - and its sine forecast damps toward a constant (corr 0.464, just under the 0.5 plausibility bar; GP/AutoReg/Chronos reach 0.87-0.96). This is standard ARIMA(1,1,1) statistics, not a coding bug, and trend='t' passes through and fixes the trend case (verified: slope continues 39.97 -> 44.47), but nothing in the docstrings warns that the default order flat-lines on trending data. Recommend documenting (or defaulting to trend handling).
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
tr = pd.DataFrame({'y': 0.05*np.arange(180) + 2.0 + 0.2*rng.standard_normal(180)})
fc = hyp.predict(tr, model='ARIMA', t=20)
print(float(fc['y'].std()), fc['y'].iloc[[0,-1]].tolist())
"
findings.expected: Forecast continues the upward trend (or docs state that order=(1,1,1) without trend= gives a level forecast).
findings.actual: linear_trend: fc_std_over_train_std = 0.0004, corr = -0.239, first3 = [10.916, 10.91, 10.911] (data ends ~11 and truth rises to ~12); noisy_sine corr = 0.464.

findings.title: Empty/None inputs crash with IndexError; the intended 'cannot forecast an empty dataset' guard is unreachable; empty list falls into the text pipeline
findings.description: Forecaster.fit guards `assert data is not None, ValueError('cannot forecast an empty dataset')`, but the dw funnel converts None and pd.DataFrame() into empty DataFrames before fit sees them, so the guard never fires and users get 'IndexError: index -1 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0' from resolve_t instead. An empty LIST is even stranger: it is routed into the text-embedding pipeline (printed 'loading corpus: minipedia...done!', i.e. a corpus download) and dies inside sklearn LDA: 'ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation.' A DataFrame with a string column dies with the raw 'ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'a''. All should produce one clear hypertools-level message.
findings.repro:

hyp.predict(pd.DataFrame(), model='Laplace', t=3)
"

findings.actual: IndexError: index -1 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0 ; empty list -> ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation.

findings.title: Input validation via `assert cond, ValueError(...)` raises AssertionError (wrong type) and vanishes under python -O
findings.description: Several user-reachable validations use the `assert cond, ValueError(msg)` anti-pattern, so callers get AssertionError (uncatchable as ValueError) and the checks are stripped entirely under `python -O`, letting execution continue into stranger downstream failures. Observed live: 'AssertionError: AutoRegressor needs more than lags=10 observations to fit; got 3' (autoreg.py fitter), 'AssertionError: unknown model: 'NopeRegressor'; supported string names are [...]' (autoreg.py _resolve_estimator), 'AssertionError: cannot infer a timestep: all observations share one timestamp' (common.py _infer_step). Same pattern (not individually triggered) in common.py fit() ('cannot forecast an empty dataset', 'fit function must return a dictionary', 'one or more required fields not returned') and autoreg.py applier. The QC pass already converted ONE of these (resolve_t's DatetimeIndex check, comment 'a real raise ... stripped under python -O') - the same reasoning applies to the rest.
findings.expected: ValueError raised (and validation active under python -O).
findings.actual: AssertionError leaked: AutoRegressor needs more than lags=10 observations to fit; got 3

findings.title: Kalman/GaussianProcess silently ignore unknown kwargs (typos like n_itr=50 change nothing, no warning) while ARIMA/AutoRegressor raise
findings.description: Kalman and GP fitters read their options via kwargs.get(...), so any misspelled option (n_itr=50, kernle=..., em_vars=...) is silently swallowed - the run 'succeeds' with default settings and zero warnings, a reproducibility hazard for scientists who believe they changed the model. ARIMA and AutoRegressor forward extras to the underlying constructor and fail loudly (TypeError: ... got an unexpected keyword argument 'bogus_flag'). Behavior should be consistent, ideally warn-or-raise on unconsumed kwargs.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import warnings, numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
x = pd.DataFrame({'y': np.sin(np.arange(100)/5.0)})
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    hyp.predict(x, model='Kalman', t=3, n_itr=50)
    print('warnings:', len(w))
"
findings.expected: TypeError or at least a warning naming the unknown kwarg.
findings.actual: warnings: 0  (run succeeds with the default n_iter=5; ARIMA path by contrast raises TypeError: ARIMA.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'bogus_flag')

findings.title: Outer **kwargs are silently dropped when model is a fork-style dict, but merged for the params-style dict
findings.description: hyp.predict(x, model={'model': 'Kalman', 'params': {}}, n_iter=9) honors n_iter (model.n_iter == 9), but hyp.predict(x, model={'model': 'Kalman', 'kwargs': {}}, n_iter=9) silently ignores it (model.n_iter == 5): in predict.py the fork-dict branch instantiates cls(*args, **resolved['kwargs']) without merging the call-level **kwargs. The docstring only says kwargs are 'ignored when model is already an instance', so users have no reason to expect the canonical (non-deprecated!) dict form to drop them while the deprecated form merges them.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
x = pd.DataFrame({'y': np.sin(np.arange(60)/5.0)})
_, m = hyp.predict(x, model={'model': 'Kalman', 'kwargs': {}}, t=3, n_iter=9, return_model=True)
print('fork-form n_iter:', m.n_iter)
"
findings.expected: fork-form n_iter: 9 (or a loud error/warning that call-level kwargs conflict with the dict spec).

findings.title: NaN handling is inconsistent across forecasters; Laplace dies with a BLANK AssertionError; all-NaN input yields a silent fabricated 0.0 forecast
findings.description: With a few NaNs in a 100-point series: Kalman, ARIMA, and Chronos forecast fine; GaussianProcess raises sklearn's 'ValueError: Input y contains NaN.'; AutoRegressor raises sklearn's long Ridge-NaN message; Laplace raises literally 'AssertionError: ' with an EMPTY message from deep inside skaters - no hint that NaNs are the cause. An all-NaN column through Kalman silently returns a forecast of exact 0.0s (masked EM with zero information fabricates zeros, no warning). Only kalman.py documents its NaN behavior; per-model NaN support/limits should be documented and errors normalized (e.g. 'Laplace cannot handle missing values; run hyp.impute first').
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
x = pd.DataFrame({'y': np.sin(np.arange(100)/5.0)})
x.iloc[[10, 40, 41, 70], 0] = np.nan
hyp.predict(x, model='Laplace', t=5)
"
findings.expected: Either a NaN-tolerant forecast or a clear error naming NaN as the problem and pointing at hyp.impute / dropna.
findings.actual: AssertionError:      (empty message; GP: 'ValueError: Input y contains NaN.'; all-NaN Kalman: [[0.0],[0.0],[0.0]] with no warning)

findings.title: Laplace forecaster is extremely slow at larger horizons (23.5 s for t=100 on a single 200-row column) and per-column cost is undocumented
findings.description: skaters' laplace(k) closure cost grows with k for every observation fed through it: t=20 on 180x1 already takes ~2 s (peers <0.35 s), and t=100 on 200x1 takes 23.5 s - roughly 1000x ARIMA/GP for the same job, and multiplied per column for multivariate data (a 10-column dataset at t=100 would be ~4 minutes). The laplace.py module docstring describes chunking verification in detail but never mentions the cost profile. Deserves a docstring performance note (and possibly a progress indicator).
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import time, numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
big = pd.DataFrame({'y': np.sin(np.arange(200)/8.0)})
t0 = time.time(); fc = hyp.predict(big, model='Laplace', t=100)
print(round(time.time()-t0, 1), 'seconds', fc.shape)
"
findings.expected: Seconds comparable to other classical models, or a documented warning about O(k*n) per-column cost.
findings.actual: 23.5 seconds (100, 1)   [ARIMA: 0.01 s, GP: 0.02 s on comparable input]

findings.title: Passing model_kwargs={...} to AutoRegressor (as its fitter docstring documents) double-nests and crashes inside sklearn
findings.description: autoreg.fitter's docstring documents "`model_kwargs` : dict, passed to `model` when it is a string or class", but AutoRegressor.__init__(model='Ridge', lags=10, **model_kwargs) captures an EXPLICIT model_kwargs= argument INSIDE the **model_kwargs catch-all, producing {'model_kwargs': {...}} which is then splatted into the sklearn constructor: TypeError: RandomForestRegressor.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'model_kwargs'. The working spelling is flat kwargs ({'model': 'RandomForestRegressor', 'lags': 5, 'random_state': 0}) - verified working and seed-deterministic - but nothing tells the user, and the two docstrings (fitter vs class) describe different calling conventions.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
x = pd.DataFrame({'y': np.sin(np.arange(100)/5.0)})
hyp.predict(x, model={'model': 'AutoRegressor', 'kwargs': {'model': 'RandomForestRegressor', 'model_kwargs': {'random_state': 0}}}, t=3)
"
findings.expected: Either model_kwargs= accepted as the documented dict, or a clear error explaining that estimator options are passed flat.
findings.actual: TypeError: RandomForestRegressor.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'model_kwargs'

findings.title: AutoRegressor's inner-estimator kwarg is named 'model', colliding with hyp.predict's own model= - the inner regressor cannot be chosen with a flat kwarg
findings.description: hyp.predict(x, model='AutoRegressor', model='SVR') is a duplicate-keyword SyntaxError, so selecting AutoRegressor's underlying sklearn regressor through the dispatcher REQUIRES the dict spec ({'model': 'AutoRegressor', 'kwargs': {'model': 'SVR'}}) or a pre-constructed instance, unlike every other forecaster option (n_iter, order, kernel, lags... all work flat). Renaming the inner kwarg (e.g. estimator=) or documenting the dict-only path would remove the trap.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
x = pd.DataFrame({'y': np.sin(np.arange(100)/5.0)})
print(hyp.predict(x, model={'model': 'AutoRegressor', 'kwargs': {'model': 'KNeighborsRegressor', 'lags': 4}}, t=3).shape)  # only working spelling
"
findings.expected: A flat spelling for choosing the inner regressor, consistent with other forecaster kwargs.
findings.actual: Flat spelling impossible (duplicate keyword 'model'); dict form works: (3, 1).

findings.title: GaussianProcess predict_new ignores the new data's VALUES entirely - reuse returns the numerically identical forecast regardless of the new dataset
findings.description: The GP applier reuses the fitted gp over the ORIGINAL time index (documented in its docstring), so hyp.predict(B, model=fitted_gp, t=5) returns values numerically IDENTICAL to continuing dataset A - even when B = A*1000 (verified: allclose true). Only B's index/columns are used. Every other reusable forecaster conditions on the new series (Kalman filters it, ARIMA .apply()s it, AutoRegressor reseeds from its tail, Laplace re-feeds it), so GP's reuse semantics are a silent odd-one-out: a scientist reusing a GP across subjects gets subject-A forecasts labeled with subject-B's index and no warning.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
t = np.arange(80)
A = pd.DataFrame({'a': np.sin(t/6.0)})
B = A * 1000.0
fcA, m = hyp.predict(A, model='GaussianProcess', t=5, return_model=True)
fcB = hyp.predict(B, model=m, t=5)
print(np.allclose(fcA.to_numpy(), fcB.to_numpy()))
"
findings.expected: Reuse conditioned on the new data (like the other models), or a runtime warning that GP reuse continues the ORIGINAL fit.
findings.actual: True  (forecast for B*1000 identical to A's continuation; no warning)

findings.title: `import hypertools.predict.kalman as k` fails with a baffling ImportError (predict submodule shadowed by the predict function)
findings.description: hypertools/__init__.py rebinds the name `predict` to the dispatcher function, shadowing the hypertools.predict subpackage as an attribute. `import hypertools.predict.kalman as k` (the `as` form walks attributes) therefore raises "ImportError: cannot import name 'kalman' from 'predict' (unknown location)". tests/predict/test_kalman.py already documents the workaround (`from hypertools.predict import kalman`), confirming this is a known sharp edge; end users hitting it get no such hint. (Same pattern presumably affects the other shadowed subpackages - only predict audited here.)
findings.expected: Module imports (or an error message explaining the function/module shadowing and the from-import workaround).
findings.actual: ImportError: cannot import name 'kalman' from 'predict' (unknown location)

findings.title: No seed control or nondeterminism documentation for stochastic forecasters (Chronos differs run-to-run; unseeded RandomForest too)
findings.description: Chronos point forecasts are sample medians and two identical hyp.predict(..., model='Chronos') calls return different values (verified: first3 -0.0922/-0.2199/-0.3192 vs -0.1182/-0.2317/-0.3263); AutoRegressor with RandomForestRegressor is likewise nondeterministic unless the user thinks to pass random_state. Nothing in predict()'s or Chronos's docstrings mentions nondeterminism, and no seed= kwarg exists. Verified workaround: torch.manual_seed(0) before each call makes Chronos exactly reproducible - exposing a seed kwarg (or documenting the torch.manual_seed recipe and random_state for sklearn estimators) would make forecasts reproducible for publication.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
x = pd.DataFrame({'y': np.sin(np.arange(180)/6.0)})
a = hyp.predict(x, model='Chronos', t=8); b = hyp.predict(x, model='Chronos', t=8)
print('identical:', np.allclose(a.to_numpy(), b.to_numpy()))
"
findings.expected: A documented seed/reproducibility story (seed kwarg, or docstring note).
findings.actual: identical: False   (with torch.manual_seed(0) before each call: identical True)

findings.title: predict_new with a different feature count than the fitted model crashes with a cryptic broadcast error
findings.description: Reusing a Kalman forecaster fit on 2 columns against 5-column new data dies inside pykalman with 'ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (5,) (2,)' - nothing names the real problem (feature-count mismatch between the fitted model and the new data) or the fix. predict_new already validates dataset COUNTS with an excellent message; a matching width check would complete it.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
_, m = hyp.predict(pd.DataFrame(rng.standard_normal((40, 2))), model='Kalman', t=3, return_model=True, n_iter=2)
hyp.predict(pd.DataFrame(rng.standard_normal((40, 5))), model=m, t=3)
"
findings.expected: ValueError naming the width mismatch, e.g. 'fitted on 2 features but new data has 5'.
findings.actual: ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (5,) (2,)

findings.title: infra: repo .venv contains a STALE non-editable hypertools install - code under test depends on the current working directory
findings.description: infra. `pip show hypertools` in the repo venv reports a NON-editable install at .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages, and 125 files differ between that copy and the repo working tree. Any python invocation whose cwd is not the repo root imports the STALE package: verified live, where model='GP' raised "unknown predict model 'GP'" and t=0 silently returned an empty (0,2) DataFrame - both bugs that the current repo source already fixes (this audit's first battery ran against the stale copy and had to be fully re-run with PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools). Anything else that executes from a non-repo cwd (tools, tutorials, notebook kernels, other audit units) is silently testing outdated code. The venv should be reinstalled with `pip install -e .` before release validation (not done here - installs are out of audit scope).
findings.repro: cd /tmp && /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools; print(hypertools.__file__)"  # -> .../site-packages/hypertools/__init__.py (stale); cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && same command -> repo tree
findings.expected: The venv resolves hypertools to the repo working tree from any cwd (editable install).
findings.actual: Location: /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages (non-editable); 125 files differ; stale copy raised ValueError: unknown predict model 'GP' and returned an empty DataFrame for t=0.
